# spotlight_runner_pool (Resource)

A pool of one-run runners: each run the pool serves gets a fresh runner of its own that ends with it. A `spotlight-host` on any machine pulls work from the pool with its token and starts a fresh sandbox for each run; install one with `curl -fsSL <spotlight>/api/install.sh | SPOTLIGHT_URL=<spotlight> SPOTLIGHT_POOL_TOKEN=<pool token> sh`. With `provision`, Spotlight pushes each run to a URL instead, whose call hands a one-run runner its credential. Writing runner pools needs a token granted the `runners` scope. Import it as `<workspace id>/<key>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
locals {
  ephemeral = {
    key           = "ephemeral"
    token_version = 1
  }
}

resource "random_password" "ephemeral" {
  length  = 48
  special = false

  keepers = local.ephemeral
}

resource "spotlight_runner_pool" "ephemeral" {
  workspace_id  = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  key           = local.ephemeral.key
  labels        = ["linux"]
  max_runs      = 8
  token         = random_password.ephemeral.result
  token_version = local.ephemeral.token_version
}

resource "random_password" "provision" {
  length  = 32
  special = false
}

resource "spotlight_runner_pool" "k8s_jobs" {
  workspace_id = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  key          = "k8s-jobs"
  labels       = ["gpu"]

  provision = {
    url            = "https://provision.example.com/runs"
    secret         = "whsec_${base64encode(random_password.provision.result)}"
    secret_version = 1
    egress         = spotlight_egress.shared.id
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `key` (String) Names the pool, as in `ephemeral`. Placement ignores it: a line or station places its work on the pool by its `labels`. It is fixed for the runner pool's life, so changing it replaces the runner pool.
- `workspace_id` (String) The workspace the runner pool belongs to. Changing it replaces the runner pool.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `labels` (Set of String) What a line or station may name in `runners` to place its work on the pool's runners, as in `linux`.
- `max_runs` (Number) The most runs the pool serves at once, from 1 to 10000. Left out, there is no limit.
- `provision` (Attributes) Makes the pool one Spotlight pushes to: it calls `url` to start a runner for each run, and the pool has no token. Left out, a `spotlight-host` pulls work from the pool with its token. Which of the two a pool does is fixed for its life, so adding or removing `provision` replaces the pool. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--provision))
- `token` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The token a `spotlight-host` serving the pool claims work with: 32 to 255 URL-safe characters, as a generated password would be. Only for a pool without `provision`. Spotlight stores only its hash. Left out, Spotlight issues one when it creates the pool, which Terraform does not store; a change to `token_version` must come with a token. Each token is single-use. Spotlight does not accept the token of another pool. A token that you rotated away, or that a deleted or replaced pool used, was used once, so no pool accepts it again, the same pool included. Thus, to rotate or replace a pool, you always need a new token. It is sent to Spotlight and never stored in the plan or the state, so it needs Terraform 1.11 or later; change `token_version` to send it again.
- `token_version` (Number) Any number; change it whenever `token` changes, so Terraform sends the new value.

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) Names the resource within its workspace, as in `ephemeral`.
- `id` (String) Issued by Spotlight when the runner pool is created, and never changed.
- `version` (Number) Rises with every change to the runner pool; each write sends it back so a change made since is not overwritten.

<a id="nestedatt--provision"></a>
### Nested Schema for `provision`

Required:

- `secret` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The secret Spotlight signs each call with, as Standard Webhooks sign: `whsec_` followed by 24 to 64 base64-encoded random bytes, as `"whsec_${base64encode(random_password.provision.result)}"` makes. It is sent to Spotlight and never stored in the plan or the state, so it needs Terraform 1.11 or later; change `secret_version` to send it again.
- `url` (String) Where Spotlight calls, over https, with each run the pool is to serve, as in `https://provision.example.com/runs`.

Optional:

- `egress` (String) The egress the pool's runners send their traffic through: `spotlight` for the egress that Spotlight operates, or the `id` of a `spotlight_egress` in the workspace. Left out, the runners have no egress, and Spotlight does not send to the pool a run that uses secrets or the Spotlight API. Changing it updates the pool in place.
- `egress_traffic` (String) Which traffic of a run goes through the egress: `all`, so egress records every connection and its allow-list applies to every host, or `bound`, only the traffic to hosts that a secret of the run is bound to. Other traffic then goes directly. Only with `egress`.
- `secret_version` (Number) Any number; change it whenever `secret` changes, so Terraform sends the new value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_runner_pool.ephemeral
  identity = {
    id = "0d6f3c1e-8a52-4f7b-9c1d-5e2a7b3f9c40"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The id Spotlight issued the runner pool when it was created.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_runner_pool.ephemeral
  id = "5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/ephemeral"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a runner pool with the id of its workspace and its key.
terraform import spotlight_runner_pool.ephemeral 5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/ephemeral
```
